output.title: When prompt sprawl is the real workflow issue
output.body:
If your AI use has started to collect little rules, exceptions, and custom instructions in different places, the problem is usually not “more AI”. It is that the workflow no longer has one clear owner or one clear source of truth. That is what I mean by prompt sprawl: the system gets harder to trust, harder to debug, and harder to hand over to someone else without a long explanation.

For a small business, the useful decision is not whether to automate everything. It is whether to stop and audit the current AI usage before you add anything new. If three people are using ChatGPT in slightly different ways, with different prompts for the same task, you already have a control problem. At that point, scaling the mess is just decorating it.

The next step is simple and manual: write down the current AI usage on one page. List the task, the prompt or instruction being used, who uses it, and where the output goes next. Do that before you try to build a pilot. It will show whether you have a real candidate for automation, or whether you first need to consolidate the way the work is being done.

That is also the kind of question a free diagnostic conversation would sort through: does AI fit this workflow at all, and if so, what is the one repeatable task worth piloting? The owner still makes the call.
